classification.archetype: Graph and compare tank models with a delayed start and a total-volume condition
classification.difficultyReason: Represent a delayed start, distinguish equal volumes from a specified combined volume, and interpret the resulting time in the physical domain.

content.prompt:
There are two tanks on a property, Tank A and Tank B.
Initially, Tank A holds $1000$ litres of water and Tank B is empty.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Tank A begins to lose water at a constant rate of $20$ litres per minute.
The volume of water in Tank A is modelled by $V = 1000 - 20t$ where $V$ is the volume in litres and $t$ is the time in minutes from when the tank begins to lose water.
On the grid below, draw the graph of this model and label it as Tank A.

spec.description: Blank graph grid for V (litres) against t (minutes). Heavy grid lines every 5 minutes and every 100 litres, finer dotted grid between them. Horizontal scale 0 to 55 labelled every 5; vertical scale 0 to 1100 labelled every 100; arrowed axes. Source image field: question. The fine dotted grid spacing (1 minute, 20 litres) is read from the image.
spec.mathematics: Empty grid, t from 0 to 55 and V from 0 to 1100, with no plotted data.
spec.answerVisibility: All grid content is permanently visible; no line is drawn.

answer.short: A straight line labelled Tank A from $(0,1000)$ to $(50,0)$.
answer.worked:
$V=1000-20t$ is linear with $V=1000$ at $t=0$ and gradient $-20$ L/min.
When $V=0$: $1000-20t=0$, so $t=50$.
Draw the straight line from $(0,1000)$ to $(50,0)$ and label it Tank A.

spec.description: The supplied grid with the line for Tank A from (0,1000) to (50,0), labelled Tank A. Source image field: solution (part a content).

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Tank B remains empty until $t = 15$ when water is added to it at a constant rate of $30$ litres per minute.
By drawing a line on the grid on the previous page, or otherwise, find the value of $t$ when the two tanks contain the same volume of water.

answer.worked:
The volume of water in Tank B is given by the equation $V = 30(t - 15)$ for $t \ge 15$.
Equating the volumes of Tank A and Tank B to find when they hold the same amount of water:
$$\begin{align*}
1000 - 20t &= 30(t - 15) \\
1000 - 20t &= 30t - 450 \\
1450 &= 50t \\
t &= 29
\end{align*}$$
This is valid since $t=29\ge 15$ and Tank A is not yet empty (it empties at $t=50$). Both tanks then hold $1000-20(29)=420$ L.

spec.description: The grid with the Tank A line, the Tank B line from (15,0) rising with gradient 30, and a dashed arrow from their intersection (29,420) down to the t-axis. Source image field: solution.
spec.mathematics: Tank A: V=1000-20t. Tank B: V=30(t-15) for t>=15. Intersection (29,420).

children.label: c
children.prompt: Using the graphs drawn, or otherwise, find the value of $t$ (where $t > 0$) when the total volume of water in the two tanks is $1000$ litres.

answer.worked:
The total volume of water in the two tanks is $1000$ litres. For $t \ge 15$, Tank B holds $30(t-15)$ litres.
$$\begin{align*}
(1000 - 20t) + 30(t - 15) &= 1000 \\
1000 - 20t + 30t - 450 &= 1000 \\
10t - 450 &= 0 \\
10t &= 450 \\
t &= 45
\end{align*}$$
For $0<t<15$ Tank B is empty and the total is $1000-20t<1000$, so there is no solution there. At $t=45$ Tank A holds $100$ L and Tank B holds $900$ L, which total $1000$ L.
Therefore, the total volume is $1000$ litres when $t = 45$ minutes.
